objective: engineer the most delicious cupcake (maximal eating quality: flavor, aroma, crumb, moistness, frosting harmony, finish)
real_world_execution_notes: The SCIENCE (food chemistry, heat transfer, emulsion physics, sensory science) is book-stable and covered by canonical references below.

The CRAFT is tacit and variable: specific flour brands/protein, oven calibration & hot spots, ambient humidity, altitude, ingredient temperature, and the eater's palate all shift outcomes; encode this variability as conflict_axes (not single right answers).

Hard tradeoffs to encode as conflict_axes/dominance_rules: moistness vs structural integrity; tenderness vs rise/doming; sweetness vs flavor complexity; cake sweetness vs frosting sweetness balance; convenience/speed vs quality; fresh-baked texture vs shelf-life.
Food safety (raw-egg products, dairy, temperature danger zone, cross-contamination, allergens) is a HARD non-negotiable dominance rule that overrides flavor/texture optimization.

domains.label: Recipe Formulation & Baking Chemistry
domains.why: Sets the ingredient skeleton: ratios and leavening chemistry determine whether the cupcake can be tender, moist, and well-risen at all. Everything downstream inherits these choices.

subdomains.label: Ingredient Ratios & Crumb Structure
subdomains.scope_hint: baker's percentages; flour/sugar/fat/egg/liquid balance; high-ratio (extra-sugar/extra-liquid) cake method; structure-builders (flour protein, egg) vs tenderizers (sugar, fat, leavening); hydration; how each ratio shift moves moistness, tenderness, rise, and shelf-life
key_books: Rose Levy Beranbaum - The Cake Bible

subdomains.label: Chemical Leavening & pH Balance
subdomains.scope_hint: baking soda vs baking powder (single/double-acting); acid-base stoichiometry; CO2 timing; pH effect on crumb color, tenderness, browning, and flavor (e.g. cocoa, buttermilk); over/under-leavening defects; altitude leavening adjustment
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking
Peter Barham - The Science of Cooking

domains.label: Batter Mixing Method & Emulsion
domains.why: How the batter is combined controls aeration, emulsion stability, and gluten development - the difference between a fine velvety crumb and a tough, tunneled, or greasy one.

subdomains.label: Mixing Methods & Aeration
subdomains.scope_hint: creaming method, reverse/two-stage (high-ratio) method, blending/muffin method, foaming/whipped-egg method; aeration mechanism (mechanical air cells as leavening nuclei); mixing time & speed; ingredient temperature; how method maps to crumb fineness and rise
key_books: Rose Levy Beranbaum - The Cake Bible
Bo Friberg - The Professional Pastry Chef

subdomains.label: Emulsion Stability & Gluten Control
subdomains.scope_hint: fat/water/egg emulsion; lecithin/egg-yolk emulsifiers; broken-batter (curdling) causes & recovery; gluten development control to avoid toughness/tunneling; overmixing vs undermixing; batter viscosity/rheology and how it sets bubble retention
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking

domains.label: Thermal Process & Oven Control
domains.why: The oven turns batter into cake: temperature, heat mode, and timing govern oven spring, doming, set point, browning, and moisture loss. Mis-baking ruins an otherwise perfect batter.

subdomains.label: Oven Thermodynamics & Setup
subdomains.scope_hint: oven calibration & true temperature; conduction/convection/radiation; preheat; rack position & hot spots; convection vs conventional; pan & liner material/color heat transfer; fill level; steam/humidity in the cavity
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking
J. Kenji Lopez-Alt - The Food Lab

subdomains.label: Oven Spring, Doming & Doneness
subdomains.scope_hint: oven spring & gas expansion; doming vs flat-top control (temperature, fill, batter viscosity); starch gelatinization & protein set point; doneness tests (springback, internal temp ~98-100C, toothpick); carryover; overflow, sinking, peaking, cracking root causes and prevention
key_books: Rose Levy Beranbaum - The Cake Bible
Peter Barham - The Science of Cooking

domains.label: Flavor Design & Sensory Balance
domains.why: Delicious is decided here: balancing sweetness/acidity/salt/bitterness/fat, layering aroma, and exploiting Maillard & caramelization so the cupcake tastes complex rather than merely sweet.

subdomains.label: Flavor Pairing & Taste Balance
subdomains.scope_hint: the five tastes + fat & aroma; sweetness moderation; salt as flavor enhancer; acidity for brightness/contrast; bitter (cocoa/coffee) for depth; flavor pairing theory & shared-aroma logic; extracts, zest, spices, fruit, chocolate systems; vanilla as rounding agent
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking
The Culinary Institute of America - Baking and Pastry

subdomains.label: Maillard, Caramelization & Aroma Development
subdomains.scope_hint: Maillard reaction & caramelization as flavor sources; browning control via pH/sugar/temperature; brown butter & toasted ingredients; aroma volatiles and how heat/storage create or lose them; layering flavor across batter, fillings, and toppings; bloom & retronasal aroma
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking
Peter Barham - The Science of Cooking

domains.label: Frosting, Filling & Finishing
domains.why: The frosting is half the bite: its type, stability, and sweetness must complement (not bury) the cake, and assembly/decoration deliver the moisture barrier, texture contrast, and visual appeal that complete deliciousness.
frontier_not_in_books: ambient-temperature buttercream stability in real service

subdomains.label: Frosting Systems & Stability
subdomains.scope_hint: American, Swiss-meringue, Italian-meringue, French, German, ermine/flour, cream-cheese buttercreams, ganache, whipped cream/stabilized; emulsion & aeration; sweetness control vs cake; texture & mouthfeel; temperature stability, splitting/seizing recovery; pairing frosting to cake flavor
key_books: Rose Levy Beranbaum - The Cake Bible
Bo Friberg - The Professional Pastry Chef

subdomains.label: Assembly, Filling, Texture Contrast & Decoration
subdomains.scope_hint: core/filling techniques (curd, jam, ganache center); frosting-to-cake ratio & balance of bite; moisture barrier & soaking syrups; piping techniques & consistency; texture/temperature contrast; garnish; visual appeal & finish; portioning a cupcake for the ideal frosting:cake ratio
key_books: Rose Levy Beranbaum - The Cake Bible
Bo Friberg - The Professional Pastry Chef
The Culinary Institute of America - Baking and Pastry

domains.label: Ingredient Selection, Quality & Substitution
domains.why: Outcome quality is bounded by ingredient quality and identity: flour protein, cocoa type, butterfat, egg freshness, sugar form, and leavener freshness set the ceiling, and principled substitutions extend reach without wrecking structure.

subdomains.label: Core Ingredient Functions & Quality
subdomains.scope_hint: flour protein & type (cake vs AP vs pastry); cocoa & chocolate (natural vs Dutch, % cacao); butterfat/water content & European-style butter; oil vs butter; egg size/freshness/temperature; sugar forms (granulated/brown/invert) & moisture; dairy (buttermilk, sour cream) & acidity; leavener freshness; salt & vanilla quality
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking

subdomains.label: Substitutions & Dietary Adaptations
subdomains.scope_hint: principled substitution (1:1 vs functional); gluten-free flour blends & binders (xanthan/psyllium); vegan egg/dairy/butter replacers (aquafaba, flax, plant butter); alternative sweeteners & fats; reduced-sugar effects; allergen handling; how each substitution shifts structure, moisture, browning, and flavor - framed as tradeoffs, not dietary/medical advice
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking
America's Test Kitchen - The How Can It Be Gluten Free Cookbook

domains.label: Sensory QC, Defect Troubleshooting & Storage
domains.why: Closes the loop: structured sensory evaluation, root-cause diagnosis of defects, and moisture/staling/safety management turn a one-off success into a repeatable, still-delicious-tomorrow cupcake.

subdomains.label: Sensory Evaluation & Defect Root-Cause
subdomains.scope_hint: structured sensory evaluation (appearance, aroma, crumb, moistness, flavor, mouthfeel, aftertaste); defect taxonomy (sinking, doming/peaking, cracking, dryness, gumminess, dense/heavy, pale, tunneling, overflow, bitter/soapy from leavening, greasy); mapping each defect to root cause across formula/mixing/bake/ingredient; corrective action loop
key_books: Rose Levy Beranbaum - The Cake Bible
Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking

subdomains.label: Moisture Retention, Staling & Food Safety
subdomains.scope_hint: moisture retention strategies (fat/sugar/invert sugar/syrups); starch retrogradation (staling) & how to slow it; shelf-life; storage & wrapping; make-ahead, refrigeration vs room-temp, freezing/thawing; food safety for egg/dairy frostings, temperature danger zone, cross-contamination, allergen labeling; serving temperature for best flavor
key_books: Harold McGee - On Food and Cooking
